title: Sermon on the Mount
desc: Jesus' great teaching on life in the kingdom of heaven.

qs.q: When Jesus went up the mountain and sat down, who came to Him to be taught?
qs.why: Seeing the crowds, Jesus went up the mountain and sat down (the posture of a teacher), and His disciples came to Him. The crowds were listening too, as 7:28 shows.

qs.q: What did Jesus say He had come to do with the Law and the Prophets?
o: Replace them with a new law
qs.why: “Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them.”

qs.q: Whose righteousness did Jesus say His hearers must surpass to enter the kingdom?
qs.why: The scribes and Pharisees were seen as the most careful law-keepers, which made the statement shocking. Jesus goes on to show that God looks at the heart, not just outward acts.

qs.q: If you remember at the altar that your brother has something against you, what should you do?
o: Leave your gift and first be reconciled
Offer a larger gift as atonement
Finish the offering, then pray for him
Ask the priest to judge between you
qs.why: Jesus puts reconciliation ahead of worship: leave the gift before the altar, go and be reconciled, then come and offer it.

qs.q: “If someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two.” What custom lies behind this?
o: Soldiers could compel civilians to carry loads
Pilgrims were escorted to the temple
Debtors had to walk to court with creditors
qs.why: Roman soldiers had the right to press local people into carrying their gear a set distance. Jesus tells His hearers to go beyond what is demanded, even for an occupying army.

qs.q: What reason does Jesus give for loving your enemies?
o: God sends sun and rain on both evil and good
Enemies will become friends in the end
It will heap shame on their heads
The Law of Moses commands it word for word
qs.why: Love your enemies “that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.”

qs.q: What do the hypocrites do when they give to the needy, according to Jesus?
o: Sound a trumpet to be honoured by men
Give only to their own relatives
Give with coins from the temple
Make the poor wait outside the gate
qs.why: They announce it in the synagogues and streets to be honoured by men, so “they already have their full reward.” Jesus says give in secret instead.

qs.q: Right after the Lord's Prayer, which line of it does Jesus explain further?
qs.why: Immediately after the prayer Jesus adds: if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not, neither will He.

qs.q: To whose splendour does Jesus compare the lilies of the field?
qs.why: Not even Solomon, the richest king of Israel, was dressed like one of these. If God clothes the grass so well, He will surely clothe His people.

qs.q: Jesus says that doing to others what you want them to do to you sums up what?
qs.why: “In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.”

qs.q: In the parable of the two builders, what made the wise man wise?
o: He heard Jesus' words and acted on them
He built higher than the floods
He built faster than the foolish man
qs.why: Both men heard the words; only the one who put them into practice built on the rock. Hearing without doing is building on sand.

qs.q: Why were the crowds astonished at the end of the sermon?
o: He taught as one with authority, unlike their scribes
He healed many during the teaching
He quoted every prophet by name
He spoke in Greek rather than Aramaic
qs.why: The scribes taught by citing earlier authorities; Jesus said “But I tell you” and taught with His own authority.

title: Gospel of Mark
desc: The fast-moving account of Jesus, the servant Son of God.

qs.q: Mark opens by quoting “Isaiah the prophet”, but the line “I will send My messenger ahead of You” comes from which prophet?
qs.why: Mark combines Malachi 3:1 (the messenger) with Isaiah 40:3 (a voice in the wilderness) under Isaiah's name. Both point to John the Baptist.

qs.q: How did the four men get the paralysed man to Jesus in Capernaum?
o: They dug through the roof and lowered him
They carried him in through a window
They waited until the crowd went home
They met Jesus on the road outside town
qs.why: The crowd blocked the door, so they uncovered the roof above Jesus and lowered the mat. Jesus saw their faith and first forgave the man's sins.

qs.q: Why did Jesus' family set out to take custody of Him?
o: They said, “He is out of His mind”
They feared Herod would arrest Him
They wanted Him back in the carpenter's shop
The Pharisees had ordered them to
qs.why: So many people pressed in that He couldn't even eat, and His family went to seize Him. Mark then sets this alongside the scribes' charge that He was possessed.

qs.q: Where was Jesus during the storm on the Sea of Galilee?
o: Asleep on a cushion in the stern
Walking toward them on the water
qs.why: He was asleep on a cushion in the stern. The disciples woke Him: “Teacher, don't You care that we are perishing?”

qs.q: After Jesus freed the demon-possessed man in the region of the Gerasenes, what did the locals do?
o: Begged Jesus to leave their region
Brought all their sick to Him
Built a shrine where it happened
Asked Him to stay and teach
qs.why: Seeing the man clothed and in his right mind, and hearing about the pigs, they were afraid and begged Jesus to leave. The healed man was sent home to tell what God had done.

qs.q: On the way to heal Jairus's daughter, who interrupted Jesus?
o: A woman who had bled for twelve years
A blind beggar by the roadside
A centurion with a sick servant
A leper who knelt before Him
qs.why: Mark sandwiches the stories: the woman suffered twelve years, and Jairus's daughter was twelve years old. The delay meant news came that the girl had died.

qs.q: Why had Herod imprisoned John the Baptist?
o: John condemned his marriage to Herodias
John refused to pay the temple tax
John led a revolt in the wilderness
John called Herod a fox in public
qs.why: Herodias had been the wife of Herod's brother Philip, and John kept saying it was not lawful. Herodias held a grudge and later got John's head.

qs.q: In Mark 7, what does “Corban” mean?
qs.why: Jesus criticises a tradition that let people declare money “Corban” (devoted to God) and so avoid supporting their parents, nullifying the command to honour them.

qs.q: What prompted Jesus to say to Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan!”?
o: Peter rebuked Him for predicting His death
Peter cut off a servant's ear
Peter wanted to build three shelters
qs.why: Just after confessing Jesus as the Christ, Peter took Him aside to rebuke Him for speaking of suffering, rejection and death. Peter had in mind the things of men, not of God.

qs.q: At Jesus' arrest, what happened to the young man wearing only a linen cloth?
o: He fled naked, leaving the cloth behind
He was arrested in Jesus' place
He ran to warn the other disciples
He followed Jesus into the high priest's house
qs.why: Only Mark records this: the guards seized him, but he left the cloth and ran. It shows how completely everyone deserted Jesus.

qs.q: Who was forced to carry Jesus' cross, and how does Mark identify him?
o: Simon of Cyrene, father of Alexander and Rufus
Joseph of Arimathea, a council member
Simon the Zealot, one of the Twelve
qs.why: He was coming in from the country. Mark names his sons, which suggests they were known to Mark's readers.

qs.q: The young man at the empty tomb told the women to take the news to the disciples and to whom by name?
qs.why: “But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee.’” Peter, who had denied Him, was singled out.

title: Genesis
desc: Beginnings: creation, the fall, and God's promises to Abraham's family.

qs.q: What work did God give the man when He placed him in the garden of Eden?
o: To guard the tree of life
qs.why: Work came before the fall: the LORD God took the man and put him in Eden to cultivate and keep it.

qs.q: Who asked “Am I my brother's keeper?”, and to whom?
qs.why: After killing Abel, Cain answered the LORD's question “Where is your brother Abel?” with a lie and this defiant question.

qs.q: Why did the people at Babel build their city and tower?
o: To make a name for themselves and not be scattered
qs.why: “Let us make a name for ourselves, that we may not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” In the next chapter God promises to make Abram's name great instead.

qs.q: After Abram rescued Lot, what did he give Melchizedek, king of Salem?
qs.why: Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, brought bread and wine and blessed Abram, and Abram gave him a tenth of everything. Hebrews 7 builds on this.

qs.q: In Genesis 15, what did Abram believe that was credited to him as righteousness?
o: God's promise of offspring like the stars
God's promise of the land of Egypt
qs.why: God took Abram outside: “Count the stars… So shall your offspring be.” Abram believed the LORD. Paul quotes this in Romans 4.

qs.q: Who called the LORD “the God who sees me”?
o: Hagar, who had fled from Sarai
qs.why: The angel of the LORD found the pregnant Hagar by a spring in the wilderness. She gave this name to the LORD who spoke to her.

qs.q: Isaac's name echoes what reaction to God's promise of a son?
qs.why: Abraham and Sarah both laughed at the promise. When Isaac was born Sarah said, “God has made me laugh.” Isaac means “he laughs.”

qs.q: Where was Abraham told to go to offer Isaac?
o: A mountain in the land of Moriah
qs.why: “Go to the land of Moriah and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains.” 2 Chronicles 3:1 places Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah.

qs.q: Why was Esau also called Edom?
o: From the red stew he traded his birthright for
From the red hair he was born with only
From the land of Edom he conquered
From his father's blessing on him
qs.why: Famished, Esau said, “Let me eat some of that red stew” — that is why he was called Edom (“red”). His descendants became the Edomites.

qs.q: Why was Jacob given the name Israel?
o: He had struggled with God and men and prevailed
He had dreamed of a stairway to heaven
He had become father of twelve sons
qs.why: After wrestling through the night at the Jabbok, Jacob would not let go without a blessing, and was renamed Israel.

qs.q: Which brother suggested selling Joseph rather than killing him?
qs.why: Reuben had already talked them out of killing Joseph, planning to rescue him. Judah then proposed selling him to the Ishmaelites: “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother?”

qs.q: When did Joseph say, “What you intended against me for evil, God intended for good”?
o: After Jacob died and his brothers feared revenge
When he first revealed himself in Egypt
When the cup was found in Benjamin's sack
When Pharaoh made him second in command
qs.why: After their father's death the brothers feared Joseph would now pay them back. He wept and reassured them of God's purpose: to preserve the lives of many people.

title: Exodus 1–20
desc: From slavery in Egypt to the covenant at Mount Sinai.

qs.q: Why did the Hebrew midwives disobey Pharaoh's order to kill the baby boys?
o: They were bribed by the Hebrews
qs.why: Shiphrah and Puah feared God and let the boys live. God was good to them and gave them families of their own.

qs.q: Who gave Moses his name, and why?
o: Pharaoh's daughter, because she drew him out of the water
His mother, because he was hidden
Miriam, because he was found by the river
Jethro, because he was a stranger
qs.why: When the child grew older he was brought to Pharaoh's daughter, who named him Moses, explaining, “I drew him out of the water.”

qs.q: Whose flock was Moses tending when he saw the burning bush?
qs.why: Moses, once a prince of Egypt, was now shepherding the flock of Jethro, the priest of Midian, when he came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

qs.q: God's words “I AM WHO I AM” answered which question from Moses?
o: What name to give if Israel asked who sent him
Why God had let Israel suffer
Where Israel was going to live
qs.why: Moses asked what to say if the Israelites asked, “What is His name?” God revealed Himself as I AM, the God of their fathers.

qs.q: How did Pharaoh first respond to Moses' request to let Israel go and worship?
o: Stopped supplying straw but kept the brick quota
qs.why: Pharaoh accused the Israelites of laziness and made them gather their own straw for the same number of bricks, turning the people against Moses.

qs.q: At which plague did Pharaoh's magicians admit, “This is the finger of God”?
qs.why: The magicians had copied the blood and frogs, but could not produce gnats from the dust. Even so, Pharaoh's heart stayed hard.

qs.q: Why did God not lead Israel along the short coastal road through Philistine country?
o: They might face war and return to Egypt
The Red Sea route was a faster road
Moses had vowed to go to Sinai first
qs.why: “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.” So God led them the roundabout way toward the Red Sea.

qs.q: Whose bones did Moses take with him out of Egypt?
qs.why: Joseph had made the Israelites swear they would carry his bones up from Egypt (Genesis 50:25). He was finally buried at Shechem (Joshua 24:32).

qs.q: Why were the Israelites to gather twice as much manna on the sixth day?
o: None would fall on the Sabbath
It would spoil after one day
Moses needed extra for the priests
A feast was held on the sixth day
qs.why: Manna kept overnight normally bred worms, but the sixth day's extra portion lasted through the Sabbath, a day of rest to the LORD.

qs.q: In the battle against Amalek at Rephidim, what decided who was winning?
o: Whether the ark went before them
Whether Joshua kept his sword drawn
qs.why: When Moses held up his hands Israel prevailed; when he lowered them Amalek prevailed. Aaron and Hur held up his hands until sunset.

qs.q: What advice did Jethro give Moses at the mountain of God?
o: Appoint capable men to judge smaller cases
Return to Egypt and free the rest
Build a tabernacle for the ark
Choose a king to lead in war
qs.why: Seeing Moses judging the people from morning to evening, Jethro said it was not good: he would wear himself out. He should teach the law and delegate.

qs.q: How does God introduce Himself before giving the Ten Commandments?
o: As the one who brought them out of Egypt
As the Creator of heaven and earth
As the judge of all the nations
qs.why: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” The law is given to people already rescued.

title: Luke
desc: An orderly account of Jesus, the Saviour of the lost.

qs.q: To whom does Luke address his Gospel, and why?
o: Theophilus, so he may know the certainty of what he was taught
The church at Antioch, to settle a dispute
Paul, to help him in Rome
qs.why: Luke says he carefully investigated everything from the beginning and wrote an orderly account for “most excellent Theophilus.”

qs.q: Why was Zechariah unable to speak until John was born?
o: He did not believe Gabriel's message
He saw the face of God in the temple
He had taken a Nazirite vow
He was struck by fear of the incense
qs.why: Gabriel said Zechariah would be silent “because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time.”

qs.q: Why did Joseph go to Bethlehem with Mary?
o: To register there as a descendant of David
To present Jesus at the temple
To find work as a builder
qs.why: Caesar Augustus ordered a census, and each went to his own town. Joseph belonged to the house and line of David, so he went to the city of David.

qs.q: Where did Mary and Joseph find twelve-year-old Jesus after three days?
o: In the temple courts among the teachers
In the house of Zechariah and Elizabeth
With travellers on the road to Nazareth
On the Mount of Olives praying
qs.why: He was sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions. “Didn't you know I had to be in My Father's house?”

qs.q: In the Nazareth synagogue, which scroll was Jesus handed to read?
qs.why: He found the place, “The Spirit of the Lord is on Me” (Isaiah 61), and said, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

qs.q: Which two Old Testament examples did Jesus cite that enraged the Nazareth synagogue?
o: The widow of Zarephath and Naaman the Syrian
Jonah in Nineveh and Rahab of Jericho
Ruth the Moabite and the queen of Sheba
Daniel in Babylon and Esther in Persia
qs.why: Both were foreigners blessed by God through Elijah and Elisha while Israel was passed over. The crowd tried to throw Jesus off a cliff.

qs.q: In whose house did a sinful woman anoint Jesus' feet in Luke 7?
qs.why: Simon the Pharisee thought a real prophet would know what kind of woman she was. Jesus answered with the parable of two debtors.

qs.q: What question led Jesus to tell the parable of the Good Samaritan?
o: “Who is the greatest in the kingdom?”
qs.why: An expert in the law, wanting to justify himself, asked this. Jesus' story made a despised Samaritan the hero.

qs.q: What prompted the parables of the lost sheep, lost coin and lost son?
o: Pharisees grumbled that Jesus ate with sinners
A rich ruler asked about eternal life
qs.why: Tax collectors and sinners were gathering to hear Him, and the Pharisees and scribes muttered. The elder brother in the third parable mirrors the grumblers.

qs.q: What did Zacchaeus promise when Jesus came to his house?
o: Half his goods to the poor and fourfold repayment
To leave his job and follow Jesus
To build a synagogue in Jericho
To pay the temple tax for all
qs.why: The crowd grumbled that Jesus was a sinner's guest. Zacchaeus stood up and promised generous restitution; Jesus said salvation had come to his house.

qs.q: What did Pilate do when he learned Jesus was a Galilean?
o: Sent Him to Herod, who was in Jerusalem
qs.why: Galilee was Herod's jurisdiction. Only Luke records that Herod and Pilate became friends that day.

qs.q: At Emmaus, when did the two disciples recognise the risen Jesus?
o: When He called them by name
qs.why: He had explained the Scriptures on the road, yet only when He took bread, blessed it and broke it were their eyes opened, and He vanished.

title: Acts
desc: The gospel spreads from Jerusalem to Rome by the power of the Spirit.

qs.q: How was Judas's replacement among the apostles chosen?
o: They prayed and cast lots; it fell to Matthias
qs.why: The candidate had to have been with them from John's baptism to the ascension. They prayed and drew lots between Joseph Barsabbas and Matthias.

qs.q: At Pentecost, which prophet did Peter quote to explain what was happening?
qs.why: Some mocked that they were drunk. Peter said it was only nine in the morning: this is what was spoken by Joel, “I will pour out My Spirit on all people.”

qs.q: What was the sin of Ananias and Sapphira?
o: Lying about keeping back part of the price
Refusing to sell their land at all
Stealing from the church's common fund
qs.why: Peter said the land and money were theirs to keep. Their sin was pretending to give all while holding some back — lying to the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: Why were the seven (including Stephen) chosen in Acts 6?
o: Greek-speaking widows were overlooked in the food
qs.why: The Hellenistic Jews complained their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution. The apostles devoted themselves to prayer and the word.

qs.q: At Stephen's stoning, at whose feet did the witnesses lay their garments?
qs.why: This is Saul's first appearance. He approved of Stephen's death and went on to ravage the church.

qs.q: What was the Ethiopian official reading when Philip met him?
o: Daniel's vision of the Son of Man
qs.why: He was reading Isaiah 53 aloud in his chariot. Starting from that Scripture, Philip told him the good news about Jesus.

qs.q: Where was Peter staying when he saw the vision of the sheet with unclean animals?
o: With Simon the tanner in Joppa
With John Mark's mother in Jerusalem
qs.why: Peter had stayed for several days in Joppa with Simon the tanner (9:43). While he prayed on the roof there, Cornelius's messengers were already on their way.

qs.q: Where were the disciples first called Christians?
qs.why: Barnabas brought Saul to Antioch, where they taught a large number for a whole year. There the disciples were first called Christians.

qs.q: What question did the Jerusalem council of Acts 15 settle?
o: Whether Gentile believers must be circumcised
Who should lead the church after James
Whether to go on mission to Spain
Whether to keep worshipping in the temple
qs.why: Men from Judea taught that Gentiles could not be saved unless circumcised. The council decided not to trouble Gentiles who were turning to God.

qs.q: Why were Paul and Silas thrown into prison in Philippi?
o: Owners of a fortune-telling slave girl lost income
They preached in the synagogue on the Sabbath
They refused to bow to Caesar's statue
The Jews of Thessalonica accused them
qs.why: Paul cast a spirit out of the girl, and her owners, seeing their profit gone, dragged them before the magistrates.

qs.q: What starting point did Paul use when speaking in Athens?
o: A statue of Zeus on the Acropolis
A recent earthquake in the city
qs.why: In the Areopagus Paul said, “What you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you,” and even quoted their own poets.

qs.q: On which island did Paul's ship run aground on the way to Rome?
qs.why: Everyone reached land safely, as Paul had foretold. On Malta Paul survived a viper bite and healed the father of Publius.

title: John
desc: Signs and words showing that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God.

qs.q: Who brought Simon Peter to Jesus?
qs.why: Andrew had heard John the Baptist call Jesus the Lamb of God. He first found Simon: “We have found the Messiah.”

qs.q: At the wedding in Cana, what were the stone water jars normally used for?
qs.why: Jesus' first sign transformed water meant for ceremonial washing into the best wine.

qs.q: Why was the Samaritan woman surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink?
o: Jews did not associate with Samaritans
qs.why: Jews and Samaritans had centuries of hostility. Jesus was crossing both ethnic and social barriers by speaking to her.

qs.q: What debate about worship did the Samaritan woman raise with Jesus?
o: Whether to worship on this mountain or in Jerusalem
Whether to offer sacrifices or prayers
Whether women could enter the temple
qs.why: Samaritans worshipped on Mount Gerizim. Jesus said a time was coming when true worshippers would worship in Spirit and in truth.

qs.q: After Jesus healed the man at the pool of Bethesda, why were the Jewish leaders upset?
o: He was carrying his mat on the Sabbath
He had gone into the pool before others
He refused to go to the priest
qs.why: The man had been ill thirty-eight years. The leaders focused on the Sabbath rule rather than the healing, and began to persecute Jesus.

qs.q: After feeding the five thousand, why did Jesus withdraw to the mountain alone?
o: They intended to make Him king by force
He was mourning John the Baptist
He was hiding from Herod's soldiers
He was tired from walking on water
qs.why: The people saw the sign and said, “This is truly the Prophet,” but wanted a political king. Jesus withdrew.

qs.q: Where did Jesus send the man born blind to wash?
qs.why: John notes that Siloam means “Sent” — fitting, since Jesus is the one sent by the Father.

qs.q: When Jesus heard Lazarus was sick, what did He do?
o: Stayed where He was two more days
qs.why: John stresses that Jesus loved Martha, Mary and Lazarus — yet He waited. By the time He arrived Lazarus had been in the tomb four days.

qs.q: After Lazarus was raised, who said it was better that one man die for the people?
o: Caiaphas, the high priest that year
qs.why: Caiaphas meant it politically, to avoid Roman reprisals, but John says he unknowingly prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation.

qs.q: Whose ear did Peter cut off in the garden?
qs.why: Only John names both Peter and Malchus. Jesus told Peter to put his sword away: “Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given Me?”

qs.q: From the cross, to whom did Jesus entrust His mother?
qs.why: “Woman, here is your son” … “Here is your mother.” From that hour this disciple took her into his home.

qs.q: When the disciples landed by the Sea of Tiberias, what did they find that recalled the night of Peter's denials?
o: A servant girl at a gate
qs.why: Peter had denied Jesus while warming himself at a charcoal fire (18:18). Beside another charcoal fire Jesus asked him three times, “Do you love Me?” and told him, “Feed My sheep.”

title: Romans
desc: Paul's great letter on the gospel of God's righteousness by faith.

qs.q: Paul says the gospel is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, “first to” whom?
o: The Jew, then to the Greek
qs.why: Paul affirms God's priority for Israel while insisting the gospel is for all who believe, Jew and Gentile alike.

qs.q: Where did Paul plan to go after visiting the Christians in Rome?
qs.why: Paul hoped to visit them on his way to Spain and be helped on his journey, after first taking a gift to the poor in Jerusalem.

qs.q: Besides Abraham, which Old Testament figure does Paul quote in Romans 4 on the blessing of forgiveness?
qs.why: Paul quotes Psalm 32: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven.”

qs.q: In Romans 4, why does it matter when Abraham's faith was credited as righteousness?
o: It was before he was circumcised
It was after he offered Isaac
It was after the Law was given
It was when he left Ur
qs.why: Righteousness came before circumcision, so Abraham is the father of all who believe, including uncircumcised Gentiles.

qs.q: In Romans 5, whom does Paul set in contrast with Christ?
qs.why: Sin and death entered through one man; grace and life come through the one man Jesus Christ. Adam was “a pattern of the One to come.”

qs.q: What objection does Paul answer at the start of Romans 6?
o: Shall we keep sinning so grace may increase?
Why does God still find fault?
qs.why: Paul had just said that where sin increased, grace increased all the more. He answers: certainly not — we died to sin.

qs.q: Which commandment does Paul use to show how the law reveals sin?
qs.why: “I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, ‘Do not covet.’” The law is holy, but sin used it.

qs.q: What does the Spirit of adoption enable believers to cry out?
qs.why: Abba is the Aramaic word for father. Believers are not slaves who fear but children and heirs.

qs.q: In Romans 9, for whom does Paul say he could wish himself cursed and cut off from Christ?
qs.why: Paul has great sorrow and unceasing anguish for his kinsmen, to whom belong the adoption, the covenants, the law and the patriarchs.

qs.q: In Paul's olive tree picture, what are the Gentile believers?
o: The root that supports the tree
Fruit that has fallen to the ground
qs.why: Gentiles share in the nourishing root. Paul warns them not to boast, since they are supported by the root, not the reverse.

qs.q: “If your enemy is hungry, feed him… you will heap burning coals on his head” — which book is Paul quoting?
qs.why: Paul quotes Proverbs 25:21–22, then sums up: do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

qs.q: Whom does Paul commend at the beginning of Romans 16?
o: Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea
Lydia, a seller of purple cloth
qs.why: Paul asks the Romans to welcome Phoebe in the Lord and assist her, for she had been a great help to many people, including Paul himself.

title: Psalms
desc: Israel's prayers and praises: lament, trust, wisdom and kingship.

qs.q: In Psalm 1, what are the wicked compared to?
o: Chaff that the wind drives away
qs.why: The righteous are like a fruitful tree by streams of water; the wicked are weightless chaff, blown away at the threshing floor.

qs.q: In Psalm 2, where has God installed His King?
qs.why: The nations rage against the LORD and His Anointed, but He laughs: “I have installed My King on Zion.” The New Testament applies this psalm to Jesus.

qs.q: According to its heading, when did David write Psalm 3?
o: When he fled from his son Absalom
When Saul hunted him at En-gedi
When he brought the ark to Jerusalem
qs.why: Though many said God would not deliver him, David could lie down and sleep, trusting the LORD.

qs.q: Which detail of Psalm 22 was fulfilled by the soldiers at the crucifixion?
o: Dividing his garments and casting lots
Offering him wine mixed with gall
Piercing his side with a spear
Breaking the legs of the others
qs.why: “They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.” John 19:24 quotes this. Jesus also cried its first line from the cross.

qs.q: In Psalm 23, where does the LORD prepare a table for the psalmist?
o: In the presence of his enemies
In the house of the LORD
In the valley of the shadow of death
qs.why: The image shifts from shepherd to host: God honours His guest openly, anointing his head with oil while enemies look on.

qs.q: In Psalm 46, “Be still, and know that I am God” comes right after God does what?
o: Makes wars cease to the ends of the earth
Calms a storm on the sea
qs.why: In context the God who makes wars cease, breaking the bow and shattering the spear, speaks: “I will be exalted among the nations.”

qs.q: What sacrifice does Psalm 51 say God will not despise?
o: A tenth of all one's income
qs.why: Written after Nathan confronted David about Bathsheba, the psalm says God does not delight in sacrifice alone; He wants a broken spirit.

qs.q: Psalm 90, which says a thousand years are but a day in God's sight, is credited to whom?
qs.why: Its heading calls it “a prayer of Moses the man of God.” It also asks, “Teach us to number our days.”

qs.q: Psalm 110 declares the king a priest forever after the order of whom?
qs.why: Kings from Judah could not be Levitical priests. Hebrews 5–7 uses this verse to explain Jesus' priesthood.

qs.q: In Psalm 118, what happens to the stone the builders rejected?
o: It is thrown into the sea
qs.why: Jesus quoted this after the parable of the tenants, and Peter preached it to the Sanhedrin (Acts 4:11).

qs.q: In Psalm 137, what did the captors in Babylon demand of the exiles?
o: To sing one of the songs of Zion
To bow down to their gods
qs.why: By the rivers of Babylon the exiles hung up their harps: “How can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?”

qs.q: In Psalm 73, what changed the psalmist's envy of the prosperous wicked?
o: He entered God's sanctuary and saw their end
qs.why: His feet had almost slipped. Only in God's presence did he understand their final destiny and say, “Whom have I in heaven but You?”

title: The big story
desc: How the Old and New Testaments fit together into one story.

qs.q: Matthew applies “Out of Egypt I called My Son” to Jesus. In Hosea, who was the “son”?
qs.why: Hosea 11:1 looks back to the exodus: “When Israel was a child, I loved him.” Matthew sees Jesus' return from Egypt retracing His people's story (Matthew 2:15).

qs.q: Jesus said, “Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness…” What happened in that episode?
o: Bitten Israelites looked at a bronze snake and lived
Moses' staff became a snake before Pharaoh
A snake tempted Israel to worship idols
Moses killed a snake that bit Aaron
qs.why: In Numbers 21 God sent snakes among the complaining people. Whoever looked at the bronze snake on a pole lived — Jesus' picture of His being lifted up on the cross (John 3:14).

qs.q: Hebrews 8 quotes at length which prophet's promise of a new covenant?
qs.why: Jeremiah 31:31–34: the law written on hearts, and sins remembered no more. Hebrews argues Jesus mediates this better covenant.

qs.q: What did Jesus mean by “the sign of the prophet Jonah”?
o: Three days and nights before coming out again
qs.why: “As Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.”

qs.q: Through which prophet did God promise David a house and kingdom that would endure forever?
qs.why: David wanted to build God a house (temple); God replied through Nathan that He would build David a house (dynasty). This Davidic covenant points to the Messiah.

qs.q: Peter argued at Pentecost that Psalm 16 (“You will not abandon my soul”) can't be only about David. Why?
o: David died, was buried, and his tomb was still there
David had been taken up to heaven
qs.why: David's tomb was in Jerusalem “to this day,” so his body did see decay. As a prophet he spoke of the resurrection of the Christ.

qs.q: Paul calls Christ “our Passover lamb” while urging the Corinthians to remove what?
qs.why: At Passover Israel cleared all leaven from their homes. Paul uses the image to tell the church to deal with sin among them.

qs.q: How does Acts link itself to another book of the New Testament?
o: It mentions a first book written to Theophilus
It names Mark as its author
It quotes John's Gospel word for word
qs.why: Both Luke and Acts are addressed to Theophilus. Acts picks up where the “first book”, about all that Jesus began to do and teach, left off.

qs.q: Ruth, the Moabite widow, was what relation to King David?
qs.why: Ruth and Boaz had Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David. Matthew 1 names her in Jesus' genealogy.

qs.q: Which woman of Jericho is praised for her faith in Hebrews 11 and her deeds in James 2?
qs.why: Rahab hid the Israelite spies (Joshua 2) and was spared when Jericho fell. Matthew 1:5 lists her as Boaz's mother.

qs.q: Malachi promised God would send Elijah before the day of the LORD. Whom did Jesus identify as this “Elijah”?
qs.why: “And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come.” Malachi 4:5 had promised Elijah before the great Day of the LORD.

qs.q: Peter calls believers “a royal priesthood, a holy nation.” Where did God first say this to Israel?
qs.why: Before giving the law, God told Israel through Moses: “unto Me you shall be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.” Peter applies it to the church (1 Peter 2:9).
